question: Bilious (green or yellow-green) vomiting in a neonate should be treated as a surgical emergency until proven otherwise.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is TRUE. Bilious vomiting in any neonate must be treated as a surgical emergency. Midgut volvulus in the setting of malrotation can cause catastrophic intestinal ischaemia within hours — do not delay surgical referral while awaiting further workup.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Bilious vomiting in a neonate indicates obstruction distal to the ampulla of Vater. Causes include malrotation with midgut volvulus (life-threatening), duodenal atresia, jejunal atresia, and Hirschsprung disease. Urgent surgical evaluation is mandatory.
